text: I cannot interview a newborn directly, so I will begin by gathering clinical details from the medical team. What is the infant's gestational age at birth, and did they experience any immediate respiratory distress upon delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the prematurity and onset of distress, I suspect Respiratory Distress Syndrome, but I need to assess severity. What are the infant's current oxygen saturation levels and respiratory rate?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The chest X-ray findings of fine reticular granulation and ground-glass appearance in a premature infant are classic for Hyaline Membrane Disease, also known as Respiratory Distress Syndrome. Given the gestational age of 33 weeks and the characteristic clinical and radiological presentation, the diagnosis is clear.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (Hyaline Membrane Disease)
